detail.title: Causal-Guided Adaptive Editing for Foundational Assumptions
detail.summary: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) enables targeted modification of foundational model premises. When integrated with incident analysis workflows, such editing helps correct systemic reasoning errors observed in diagnostic tasks like root cause analysis.
detail.reason: Synthesizing CAKE findings with RCA-specific LLM performance data to address foundational error correction.

detail.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
detail.summary: Cognitive reasoning agents designed for incident reporting, such as CRASH, demonstrate potential utility in industrial safety analysis. Incorporating unstructured knowledge editing methods allows these agents to adapt to non-standardized narrative reports by refining their internal causality maps.
detail.reason: Applying CAKE and unstructured editing frameworks to adapt specialized incident agents to general industrial domains.

children.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution

detail.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution
detail.summary: Autonomous agents often fail in reasoning tasks because of unrecognized blind spots in their training or causal graph. Causal-guided knowledge editing assists in addressing these failure states by allowing developers to explicitly map and adjust the agent's reasoning trajectory during root cause analysis workflows.
detail.reason: Investigating how meta-reasoning agents can utilize structural causal editing to self-correct reasoning limitations.
